facts.claim: The Cisco CP-9951 phone runs DOOM v.666 natively, locally, persistently, and offline using its ARMv6 CPU.
DOOM renders directly to /dev/fb1 and reads input from /dev/input/keypad0 using the physical Cisco keypad.
Sound is handled via 8 kHz G.711 μ-law RTP, relayed locally to the Cisco media system with fallback to loopback for cable-free operation.
The installation persists under /mnt/flash2/doom-v666 and is launched via http://127.0.0.1:8095/launch through Cisco’s Applications menu.
The project began with a €35 Cisco Unified IP Phone CP-9951 running stock firmware sip9951.9-2-1, with SSH access via 'default'/'cisco' credentials.
The embedded Linux system is MontaVista Linux Professional Edition Blackfoot, ARMv6, kernel 2.6.18_pro500, with 244 MB RAM and BusyBox 1.9.1.
The project transitioned from SIP-based DTMF control to a native DOOM port running directly on the phone’s ARM CPU, with physical keypad mapped to controls.
The final proof test on 15 September 2026 confirmed cold boot, offline operation, and persistent launch via Applications → Doom without Ethernet or shell access.
